correctness.rationale: Each vertex has fixed row, column, and doubly centered squared projection energies, calculated directly from its occupied row/column indicator vectors. Group invariance or the explicit four-pattern entry second moments produce the exact three covariance eigenvalues and their multiplicities. The covariance range equals the true affine direction space in all three rank regimes. Averaging constraints of any enclosing ellipsoid and applying positive-matrix arithmetic–geometric mean yields the sharp global determinant bound d^d detΣ; A=dΣ reaches equality at all vertices, proving unique optimality. Comparing the three eigenvalues and exact saturation formulas gives the complete jump direction case split. The standard-library rational checker validated 25 small full polytope instances with 1016 exact vertices plus 110920 mode-order and jump comparisons. Finite tests are supplementary.

value.rationale: Fixed-cardinality bipartite matching polytopes are canonical and already studied as transportation and nonattacking-rook models; the minimum-volume enclosing ellipsoid is a natural geometric invariant complementing their established inball, enclosing sphere, and inner John ellipsoid. Computing its full Frobenius spectrum for every rectangular parameter and its changing affine-hull dimension supplies structural information unavailable from a scalar radius or combinatorial description. The sharp exceptional saturation classification identifies a meaningful boundary phenomenon: anisotropy grows with rank before saturation but frequently falls at the last step, and for each fixed m≥3 with n→∞ the last-step factor tends to 1/(m−1). These natural, infinite-family, non-implied geometric data exceed a routine one-off parameter substitution.
